title: Framing Session — Validation Sprint Charter
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the focused scope for a two-week Validation Sprint with AcmeCorps (internal codename: Airship). Goal is to rapidly validate the end-to-end feasibility and economics of embedding-driven search and summarization flows on Redwood Inference in a production-like environment.

Primary objectives:
1) Prove the user-facing quality hypothesis: Embedding + rerank pipeline returns relevant results for 75%+ of sampled queries compared to customer baseline.
2) Prove the operational hypothesis: 95th-percentile latency for synchronous queries under target load stays below 450ms in the customer region.
3) Prove the cost hypothesis: Estimated per-query inference cost using suggested batching/quantization remains <= $0.010 for production traffic profile.

Success hypotheses (what we will test):
- H1 (Quality): For the labeled sample (n=250 queries), the new pipeline achieves at least 0.75 NDCG@10 relative to AcmeCorps’ current Elasticsearch baseline.
- H2 (Latency): With the agreed concurrency pattern (burst to 80 rps sustained for 5m windows), end-to-end p95 latency <= 450ms.
- H3 (Stability): No more than 2% request error rate (5xx + 4xx due to infra) during load tests after warmup.
- H4 (Security/Privacy): Customer-provided PII is never logged; KMS-backed key rotation works end-to-end on private deployment.

Acceptance criteria (hard gates):
- Functional: Retrieval + rerank produces non-empty results for >= 98% of user queries in the sample.
- Quality metric: NDCG@10 >= 0.75 on labeled evaluation set.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 450ms; p50 <= 120ms during steady-state.
- Cost: Modeled unit cost <= $0.010/query for 10k qps-month projection (using Redwood Optimize recommendations).
- Reliability: Error rate <= 2% during stress tests; no more than one severity-two incident.
- Compliance: Audit logs present and accessible to customer; all persistent storage tagged and encrypted.

Scope (in/out):
- In scope: Model selection and tuning, quantization experiments (int8 where applicable), embedding index creation (FAISS), query-level caching experiments, basic UI integration test harness, synthetic and real sample traffic up to agreed limits.
- Out of scope: Full production rollout automation, multi-region failover, long-term data retention policy changes, third-party data enrichment.

Key deliverables:
- Deployment artifact: terraform + manifests for a single-customer private deployment in customer staging VPC.
- Eval report: labeled dataset, NDCG/precision/recall tables, per-query failure modes and example traces.
- Performance benchmark doc: p50/p90/p95 across scenarios, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates.
- Cost model: token-level breakdown and recommended batching/caching knobs.
- Playbook: handoff notes and next-step checklist for Dedicated/Hosted migration.

Test plan (how we'll measure):
1) Data preparation: ingest customer KB subset (up to 30k docs), generate embeddings, create FAISS index. Maintain a labeled test set of 250 queries with relevance judgments.
2) Functional tests: smoke tests, end-to-end runbook (ingest -> index -> query -> rerank -> response).
3) Quality eval: calculate NDCG@k, Precision@5, and error taxonomy.
4) Load tests: two phases — warmup (ramp to 20 rps) then stress (burst to 80 rps sustained 5m). Capture latency distribution and error rates.
5) Cost simulation: replay sampled traffic through the Optimize profile to produce a 30-day cost projection.

Data & security requirements:
- Customer dataset will be accessed in a staging environment only; no exports allowed.
- Encryption: all volumes encrypted with customer-managed KMS key.
- Logging: redact PII from traces; retain only request-level metadata for debugging.
- Compliance: record the checklist for jurisdictional data residency (EU vs US) and document control plane interactions.

Deployment and rollout timeline (14 calendar days):
Day 0 (pre): legal + NDAs signed; access tokens + KMS key exchange; sample data received.
Day 1: Architecture alignment workshop (30–45m) with engineering + customer devs; confirm test harness.
Day 2–4: Staging deployment + model onboarding; embedding build and index creation.
Day 5: Functional end-to-end smoke tests; triage issues.
Day 6–8: Quality tuning loop (reranker params, prompt templates), labeled eval runs.
Day 9: Performance warmup runs; iterate on batching & cache config.
Day 10: Stress tests and cost simulation; capture metrics.
Day 11: Mitigation window for issues discovered in stress.
Day 12: Final acceptance run with customer observers; collect sign-off artifacts.
Day 13: Post-run analysis; draft final evaluation report.
Day 14: Handoff meeting — deliverables, recommendations, and next-step decision (scale, extend, or stop).

Roles and contacts:
- Solutions lead (SE): Aisha Patel — overall sprint owner, customer syncs.
- ML engineer: Mateo Ruiz — model tuning, eval metrics.
- Platform engineer: Claire Huang — deployment manifests, infra.
- Customer technical lead: Jordan Mills (AcmeCorps).
- SRE on-call: Devon O'Neil — runbooks and incident response.

Communication plan:
- Primary channel: Slack #se-airship (invite customer observers).
- Weekly checkpoints: 15m daily stand for first week, 30m demo on Day 7 and Day 14.
- Emergency paging: SRE rotation list shared with customer.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Customer sample data contains unexpected formats causing embedding failures.
  Mitigation: Pre-flight data validation script; fallback to tokenized placeholder and manual triage.
- Risk: p95 latency >> target due to cold KV cache.
  Mitigation: Warm-up strategy, synthetic prefix caching, adjust batch sizes, consider smaller model variant for tail latency.
- Risk: Cost projection exceeds target after accounting for real traffic distribution.
  Mitigation: Run cost sensitivity matrix and propose quantization + batching tradeoff.

Meeting agenda (Day 1 architecture alignment):
- 0–5m: Introductions and scope recap.
- 5–15m: Review success hypotheses and acceptance criteria.
- 15–25m: Architecture walkthrough (ingest, embeddings, index, rerank, API surface).
- 25–35m: Security & data handling confirmation (KMS, VPC, logs).
- 35–40m: Timeline and next steps; assign immediate action items.

Appendix — quick debug checklist (for first 24h):
- Verify service account access and KMS decryption of sample blob.
- Run sample ingest script (ingest-check.sh) and confirm 30k doc index creation completes < 45m.
- Confirm embedding model matches agreed version and dimension size.
- Verify API key rotation via staging key and that logs are present.

Notes to self: keep the labeled queries small but representative; avoid overfitting reranker to the 250-sample during the sprint. Focus on reproducible experiments and commit scripts into the poc-scripts repo with clear tags.

Decision points after sprint (binary):
- Move to Dedicated if cost model and latency targets met and customer needs sustained throughput.
- Propose Hosted pilot if quick time-to-market favored and data residency not strict.
- Recommend Private deployment with longer proof if regulatory controls or KMS isolation required.

Deliver this doc to customer a day before Day 1 workshop and ask for confirmation of acceptance criteria and labeled query set within 48 hours.
